title: The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids
text:
A mother goat had seven young kids. One day she had to go into the forest for food, and she warned them: do not open the door to the wolf. You will know him by his rough voice and his black feet.

Soon there was a knock. "Open up, children, your mother is back," said a rough voice. The kids refused: their mother's voice was soft. The wolf went and ate a lump of chalk to soften his voice. When he came back, he put a black paw on the windowsill, and again they refused. He made a baker spread dough on his paw and a miller dust it with white flour. The third time, his voice was soft and his paw was white, and the kids opened the door.

The wolf swallowed six of them, one after another. Only the youngest, hiding in the clock case, escaped. The wolf lay down in the meadow and fell asleep.

When the mother returned, the youngest told her everything. She found the wolf snoring, cut open his belly with scissors, and out jumped all six kids alive, for in his greed he had swallowed them whole. They filled his belly with stones and sewed it up. When the wolf woke, thirsty, he went to the well, leaned over, and the stones pulled him in.
lesson: Warnings only protect children if they remember them under pressure. Teach the reasons behind the rules, because a clever threat will look different each time.
people: The mother goat, her seven kids, the wolf
source: Brothers Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 5 (Der Wolf und die sieben jungen Geisslein)
